answer: Commit-reveal proof-of-work resists sybils: minting requires committing to a puzzle solution in one epoch and revealing it the next, so the work cannot be pipelined or precomputed on demand — a ripple that must cross two epochs per identity. A farm cannot mint a harbor of keys instantly; each needs the commit-then-reveal latency, and the kernel of the defense is that the reveal binds to the prior commit's epoch seed. Honest agents pay the two-phase cost once; a swarm pays it per head with no batching across the phase boundary.
